note: S14b.4 SIGN-OFF #3 (spec §10.6): a remove_line that touches a promoted region is REJECTED (reject-by-default; demote first). Scene: [v@500 full, h@500[0,500] id:2, h@500[500,1000] id:3] with the LEFT column {0,0,500,1000} promoted (its interior line-set is h@500[0,500] id:2). TWO cases in one fixture: (REJECT) remove_line(id:2) — id:2 is INTERIOR to the left promotion's coord_map → {ok:false} with the sign-off #3 promotion-aware reason, store INTACT (no arr surfaced, jq purity). (ALLOW) remove_line(id:3) — id:3 is the RIGHT column's interior, EXTERIOR to the left promotion → falls through the guard and proceeds through S14a (incident=2, sides form a rectangle) → {ok:true}. The guard is STRUCTURAL (interior-to/on-face-of coord_map), NOT valid_rec-delegated: an un-rectangling removal silently re-merges to a coarser-but-VALID cell (valid_rec:true) and a residual dangling line union-finds to ONE valid cell, so neither valid_rec nor a re-run-valid check is reliable teeth — the geometric structural rule is. NOTE (constructibility correction to the locked design prose): the design framed the unique teeth as interior removals S14a ALLOWS (incident==2) that un-rectangle a promotion; that exact case is NOT constructible (orphaning another line requires a T-junction ⇒ incident≥3 ⇒ S14a's _sides_form_rectangle already rejects). So the guard is spliced BEFORE _sides_form_rectangle and rejects any promotion-touching removal with the promotion-aware reason. Builds on S14a's remove_line_lshape_reject — same guard machinery, now promotion-aware.

expect.reject_reason: remove_line: rejected — line is inside/bounding a promoted region (would un-rectangle its line-set; demote first to dissolve) [sign-off #3]
